mainEntity.name: How do texture repairs differ in older or historic Jerome homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Historic homes in hillside communities like Jerome often feature underlying plaster, wood lath, or heavy settling cracks rather than standard modern drywall. Patching orange-peel texture over plaster requires stabilizing the backing, anchoring loose substrate, and using flexible setting-type compounds. Standard drywall mud alone may crack along old movement lines, so repairs in older regional structures often demand deeper structural prep before texture blending begins.
